Thrilled to have Deputy Secretary of Labor @Sonderling47 here in #CO08 as we highlight the cutting-edge work happening at @aimscc.

I’m proud to work alongside this administration to embrace the future of AI and keep American workers at the center of innovation. https://t.co/ymnnkgigIA

Love it or hate it, AI is here to stay.

And let me be clear — it’s a race America must win. https://t.co/5loh0OguBB
If you’re nervous about AI, you need to be terrified about communist China becoming the global leader in AI because it was driven out of places like Colorado as a result of Colorado’s AI law.

AI is a game changing technology, and there can be only one global leader. If America does not win the AI race, communist China will.

I joined @RepLangworthy in sending Howard Lutnick, the US Secretary of Commerce a letter highlighting concerns with burdensome state AI regulations, urging a coherent national framework that protects consumers without stopping innovation.

Like it or not, artificial intelligence is here to stay. The U.S. can choose to lead the world in this transformative technology or we can regulate it into the hands of Communist China. If we care about American jobs, national security and staying ahead of our foreign adversaries, we need a smart, consistent national approach that keeps innovation here at home

AI is poised to be among the most transformative technologies of our generation, with profound implications for American economic growth, competitiveness, and national security. The United States must lead in the development and deployment of these technologies, or we risk ceding future economic growth and global AI dominance to the Chinese Communist Party.

Today, I introduced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act.

As AI data centers drive demand for new power plants and grid upgrades, Colorado families shouldn't be stuck paying the bill.

This legislation helps ensure large data centers pay for the infrastructure they require — protecting ratepayers while supporting American innovation and energy security.

I couldn’t agree more. America cannot afford to fall behind Communist China in the race for AI.

We need commonsense federal guardrails that protect Americans without crushing innovation.

That’s why I introduced the Open Source AI Leadership Act—to strengthen U.S. leadership in open source AI while identifying the risks posed by CCP-controlled models. ⬇️

The race for AI leadership is a race America cannot afford to lose. Communist China is working every day to outcompete us, steal American innovation, and expand its technological influence around the world. We should be making it easier for our nation's innovators and startups to build, compete, and lead. This bill helps unleash American open-source AI while implementing common sense consumer protections. It also creates safeguard to identify and counter national security threats from foreign adversaries.

America needs the digital infrastructure to win the AI race against Communist China — but Colorado families shouldn’t be forced to give up their water or pay higher utility bills to make it happen.

We can lead in AI AND develop data centers responsibly.

That’s why I introduced the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act to make sure the companies creating massive new electricity demand pay for the infrastructure they need — not Colorado families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses.

American small businesses shouldn’t have to rely on Chinese Communist Party-linked AI models to compete.

My Open-Source AI Leadership Act promotes American alternatives while exposing the security risks posed by Chinese AI.

American data belongs in America — not in the hands of Communist China. We need to protect our innovators, our jobs, and our data. 🇺🇸

This week, my bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act is heading to the House floor.

America can beat China in the AI race without forcing families and small businesses to foot the bill for the massive energy demands of data centers.

I’m urging my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support this commonsense bill and protect American ratepayers.

This issue is only becoming more important as the global race for artificial intelligence accelerates.

Communist China is working every day to outcompete the United States, wage cyberwar, steal American innovation and information, and expand its technological influence around the world. America cannot afford to lose that race.

Today, my bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act passed the House!

America can lead the world in AI without forcing families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses to foot the bill for the massive energy demands of data centers.

Thank you to my colleagues on both sides of the aisle for coming together to protect American ratepayers and keep American innovation moving forward. 🇺🇸

But with that growth our demand for energy is also skyrocketing, and some people have very understandable reservations and questions about data centers. We cannot accelerate this growth on the back of Americans working hard to pay for electric bills at the end of the month.
There’s clearly a space here for Congress to act, but we have to act with the understanding that if the United States is not the leader in this, then China will become the leader in this.

A lot of the technology keeping America safe is being built right here in Colorado. 🇺🇸🛰️

I checked back in with the team at Vantor’s headquarters to get an update on their work and see how Colorado innovation in satellite imagery, AI, and geospatial intelligence is supporting our warfighters and strengthening our national security.

As China and Russia challenge us on Earth and in space, America cannot afford to fall behind. We need to invest in American innovation and make sure our warfighters have the best technology in the world.

From the Ratepayer Protection Act to the KIDS Act and Open Source AI Leadership Act, I’m fighting for commonsense federal guardrails around AI that protect our kids, families, and wallets — without surrendering America’s edge to Communist China. https://t.co/y00D4JjIEt
